medium_value.description: Resolve the edit-scope conflict before implementation: explicitly authorize .loa-version.json and README changes or remove those edits from Task 3.5. Enumerate any additional paths required by bead closure and release tooling.
Specify batch randomization or counterbalancing across arms and trials, including its seed and scheduling constraints, and record realized execution order and timestamps.
Define how partial groups and --run-cap 30 interact with balanced arm pairs, trial completion, resume, information fractions, and look eligibility. Test interruption at the cap between paired cells.

Add registered terminal outcomes for fewer than six valid PRs, zero valid pairs, unavailable later looks, and a cap reached before any eligible look. Require final reporting to preserve these outcomes without inventing a boundary decision.
Run and record the G1 positive-control verdict before the primary look, then define operational behavior for failed, void, and unexercised controls, including whether later batches are launched.
Define explicit stop, repair, and re-registration procedures for an out-of-band existing-row placebo, and specify how a failed new-row placebo changes the final verdict and release evidence.

Freeze the judge sampling universe and specify how omitted findings are sampled alongside emitted findings. Require positive inclusion probability for every unit needed to estimate corrected recall, and record probabilities for each sampling stage.

Specify the live reproduction sample, comparison statistic, expected variability, and discrepancy handling before execution. Separate exact artifact reproduction from stochastic live-rerun acceptance.

Move end-to-end goal validation before version cutting, merge, and archive. Make unresolved reproduction mismatches explicit blockers for the proof gate, and rerun affected verification after any review or Bridgebuilder code changes.

Add independent reference checks and simulation acceptance thresholds for the complete sequential procedure, including null false-positive rate, interval coverage at stopping, and decision frequencies under alternative effects and correlated sessions.

Define a failure policy for incomplete incident-source retrieval: retries, completeness thresholds, fixture eligibility, and required missing-source caveats. Include a test where one paginated source fails after returning partial results.

Add an explicit Sprint 1 implementation task for judge-sample.sh, its packet format, deterministic strata selection, inclusion probabilities, and judge-sample.bats. Make Task 2.6 depend on its acceptance tests.
Create and verify a preliminary record branch before Task 3.3, then update it with reproduction evidence after verification. Specify the exact commits cloned and the final evidence inclusion list.

Add a runner task and tests for atomic spend reservations, concurrent launches, retry charges, reservation reconciliation, and cap enforcement. Define whether the cap includes smoke, open-mount controls, blind sessions, and live reproduction, and reserve required downstream spend before batches start.
Define a single attempt-limit rule using explicit initial-attempt and retry counts, and use it consistently in runner behavior, metadata, resume logic, and tests.

Define annotation units and the negative sampling frame before computing kappa, including how independently discovered defects are aligned, how absent findings are represented, and how localization and grouping disagreements enter each statistic.

Separate independent head-code annotation from incident-assisted supplementation, or explicitly label incident-assisted ground truth. Freeze and report label provenance by stage, and audit incident packets for feedback-derived findings before blind annotation.

Make the codebook pilot a separate calibration fixture excluded from confirmatory selection, or explicitly register its reuse and exposure. Freeze the codebook before selected-fixture annotation begins.

Register objective eligibility criteria, spare activation conditions, replacement order, and a cutoff after which replacement is forbidden. Preserve every exclusion and replacement in a candidate disposition table.

Bind the execution commit and container image digest into a verifiable registration chain before smoke. Define how Sprint 2 freezing can occur without changing registered input hashes and require rejection of unregistered code or image changes.

Split the record-branch step so the batch run directories, packets, labels and transcripts are pushed to the record branch before Task 3.3 runs, and the reproduction report is appended in a second push during Task 3.6. State in REPRODUCE.md which branch/commit supplies the code (cycle branch pin) and which supplies the results (record branch).
Fix the placebo band numerically in Task 1.8 (a constant with a unit test, or a DEC row) before Task 1.10 executes, and state in Task 1.10 that the band predates the run.

Turn the codebook trial ('tried on one fixture first and revised before the blind run') into an explicit step of Task 1.3 or 1.6, name the trial fixture, and state that it is either excluded from the primary set or re-annotated blind under the final codebook with the trial labels discarded.

Bind the harness code to the registration: either include the harness tree hash (evals/) in REGISTRATION.json at Task 1.11, or require a registration addendum recording the Sprint 2 pin before the smoke in Task 2.1, with any post-pin harness fix recorded as an addendum.

Specify how the c131 suite root's MANIFEST.sha256 is handled after the git mv migration changes its task.yaml paths (refreeze with a DEC row, or leave paths and add a compatibility lookup), and confirm the change passes the G-7 allowlisted-diff check.
Add a pilot judge pass on a seeded subsample of G1 rows immediately after look 1 (before Task 2.4 launches), with the full stratified sample in Task 2.6 still drawn over the final universe.

Record the annotator and judge model IDs and pins in annotation/result.md, judge/result.md and REGISTRATION.json, and either diversify the two blind annotators (different model or prompt variant) or state in PREREGISTRATION.md that kappa is an intra-model agreement figure.

Add the Codex credential expiry (2026-10-28T04:44Z) as a Sprint 3 dependency for the live rerun in Task 3.3, with a fallback (refresh procedure or 'sampled rerun deferred' note in the reproduction report).
Add a gate before Task 3.6 that PR #1288 is merged to main (or that the cycle PR is rebased to include it), since the archive step depends on the fixed archive-cycle.sh being on main.

Define a smoke-level halt criterion in Task 2.2 and PREREGISTRATION.md: if realized cost ratios fall outside the dollar-matching tolerance for more than a stated share of PRs, or more than the spare count fail the closed mount, stop before G1 and record the apparatus finding.

Pre-register a judge agreement floor (kappa or corrected recall gap) and its consequence for the primary read (caveat, sensitivity, or void), listed under 'judge protocol' in Task 1.11 and checked in Task 3.1.
Move Task 3.E2E ahead of Task 3.5 (release cut) and Task 3.6 (merge, record branch, archive) in the dependency chain, and make a passing e2e.md a precondition of the rc.7 CHANGELOG heading.
Reorder Task 2.3 so the positive-control read precedes reads-c132.py --look 1, matching the Sprint 2 acceptance criterion.

Rewrite the record-branch content list in Task 3.6 as explicit include and exclude lists (exclude: sandboxes; include: batch records, packets, labels, blind-session transcripts, judge files, reproduction report).
Align the Sprint 2 Codex-expiry mitigation ('schedule to finish by 10-27') with the Sprint 2 end date (10-25), or state that 10-27 refers to the Sprint 3 live rerun.

Add a Sprint 1 scope-split rule: name the deliverables that may slip into a sprint-1b (e.g., 1.7a–c runner changes) without blocking registration, and the ones that must land before the hash (1.1–1.6, 1.8–1.11). Add a 'Sprint 1 overrun' row to the Risk Register.

Add a Sprint 1 task (or extend Task 1.8) that builds judge-sample.sh (seeded stratified sampler, inclusion probabilities, arm/decision-free packets) and evals/tests/judge-sample.bats, and add the FR-4 AC 1 determinism criterion to Sprint 1 Acceptance Criteria.

Replace the hard-coded '× 2 trials', 'concurrency 3' and '--run-cap 30' in Task 2.3 with references to the registered values (REGISTRATION.json trials/k, cap, reservation rule), or state explicitly how --run-cap relates to the registered cap and that trials come from power.md.

State the size of the exposure-clean candidate pool, add a pool-bounded-N rule alongside the affordable-N rule, and define what happens when more than the 2 spares are lost to annotation failure, head non-resolution or smoke mount failure (e.g., annotate the whole unseen pool in Task 1.6 so substitution in seeded order is always possible, or declare the study continues at reduced N with achieved power stated).

Add a pre-registered rule for G2/G3 launch when the G1 positive control reads void or 'not exercised': halt further arm spend and ship the apparatus finding, or run one retry of the open-mount arm on G1 before continuing. Put this in the PREREGISTRATION.md content list of Task 1.11 and as a gate in Task 2.4.

Run the placebo on the new rows (Task 3.4) before or as the first step of Task 3.1, so the placebo band verdict exists before the final-read DEC rows are written and before the report is drafted; update the dependency chain to 3.4 → 3.1 → 3.2 → 3.3.

State what the registered cap covers (arm spend only, or all model spend), and give estimates for non-arm model spend: blind annotation sessions (2 × (N+2)), judge sessions, the ≈USD 60 reproducer rerun, and implementer worktree sessions. Have the affordable-N rule in Task 1.9 subtract these from the USD 2,500 envelope.

Make the Task 1.9 → Task 1.6 dependency explicit in the Dependencies Map and name the Sprint 1 critical path (1.8 → 1.9 → 1.6 → 1.11), or decouple the annotation set from N by annotating a pre-declared pool so 1.6 can start after 1.3–1.5.

Assign single ownership for the grader label_set/labels_meta change (currently listed under both Task 1.5 and Task 1.7b) and for seed-corpus-from-record.sh edits (Task 1.1 adds --feedback and exposure; Task 1.5 adds the v2 header), and sequence those tasks instead of listing them as parallel.

blockers.concern: Matched-cell validity requires all sessions to land, while other arms may require fewer sessions; the plan does not specify an analysis that addresses this asymmetric missingness.
blockers.why_matters: Larger-k cells have more opportunities to fail, so complete-case comparisons can select easier PRs or more compliant runs and bias the primary estimate.
blockers.location: Tasks 1.7a–b; Task 1.8 validity filter; Sprint 2 matched-cell degradation
blockers.recommendation: Pre-register paired inclusion rules, report missingness by arm and k, and require sensitivity bounds or an intention-to-run analysis showing how failed sessions affect the conclusion.

blockers.concern: Quoting third-party text in fences is treated as preventing interpretation, and transcript taint checks are used without an explicit network or filesystem enforcement requirement.
blockers.why_matters: Issue bodies and repository content can contain prompt injection; a container with credentials can leak data or access labels before a transcript check detects anything.
blockers.recommendation: Enforce packet-only filesystem access and restricted network destinations at runtime, expose only necessary credentials through a controlled mechanism, and test adversarial packet content plus out-of-band access attempts.

blockers.concern: Task 3.3's reproduction (hash table, sampled rerun) precedes Task 3.6, which triages a Bridgebuilder round and fixes findings before merge. Any code or data fix in 3.6 invalidates the proof hashes from 3.3, and the record branch (which the reproducer clones) is built before 3.6 yet must also contain the reproduction report.
blockers.why_matters: G-6 'Proof' can be true at 3.3 and false at merge. The record branch would carry a reproduction report that no longer matches the shipped code, which is the exact failure the cycle exists to rule out.
blockers.location: Sprint 3 Tasks 3.3, 3.6; Dependencies Map (3.3/3.4 → 3.5 → 3.6); Sprint 3 Dependencies
blockers.recommendation: Make the record branch a two-stage artefact: stage 1 (batch records, labels, analysis) before 3.3; stage 2 appends the reproduction report. Add an explicit rule: any post-3.3 change to `evals/analysis/c132/`, the grader, rows, or manifests re-triggers `reproduce.sh` and re-hashes before the rc.7 heading is written; restrict Bridgebuilder fixes outside those paths or re-run the proof.

blockers.concern: Task 3.5 changes .loa-version.json and the README pin, but the cycle authorizes edits only to evals/, grimoires/, and CHANGELOG.md.
blockers.why_matters: Completing the release as written would violate the declared change boundary and potentially invalidate G-7.
blockers.recommendation: Resolve the scope conflict before implementation by explicitly authorizing the release metadata changes or removing them from this cycle, and make the allowed-path check enforce the resulting scope.

blockers.concern: The cap's accounting scope is unclear: Phase 0 blind sessions and planning calls occur before Task 1.9 sets the binding cap, while judging and live reproduction also consume money.
blockers.why_matters: The study can satisfy an arm-spend cap while exceeding the overall USD 2,500 envelope or exhausting funds before the required proof.
blockers.recommendation: Define separate total-cycle and arm budgets before paid work, enumerate included costs, and reserve funds for annotation, judging, controls, retries, and reproduction before choosing affordable N.

blockers.concern: The fresh-clone reproduction depends on a record branch whose creation and push are scheduled in Task 3.6, after reproduction in Task 3.3.
blockers.why_matters: The proof cannot run in the specified order, and an unspecified provisional branch could omit artifacts needed to reproduce the results.
blockers.recommendation: Add an explicit pre-reproduction task that builds, scans, pushes, and pins an immutable evidence commit containing all required run artifacts; reproduce that exact commit and later append the proof.

blockers.concern: The judge protocol does not explicitly require sampling missed ground-truth defects as well as emitted findings.
blockers.why_matters: A judge that sees only emitted findings can validate precision but cannot identify grader false negatives or justify corrected recall through Horvitz–Thompson weighting.
blockers.location: Task 2.6; judge_agree.py; PRD FR-4 acceptance criteria
blockers.recommendation: Define separate sampling universes for findings and ground-truth defect opportunities, give every relevant unit a known nonzero inclusion probability, and test corrected recall and precision against a fully judged synthetic population.

blockers.concern: The packet construction uses fix hunks and incidents, but it does not explicitly establish how defects omitted from those sources enter the ground truth.
blockers.why_matters: Both blind annotators can agree on an incomplete candidate set, preferentially measuring previously discovered defects while misclassifying novel valid findings as false positives.
blockers.recommendation: Define the target defect universe explicitly, include an independent discovery pass over the original change, and freeze a blinded procedure for adjudicating valid findings absent from the initial manifest.

blockers.concern: The plan allows cap-driven partial groups and validity-driven exclusions to enter interim looks without explicitly requiring calibration under those data-dependent completion mechanisms.
blockers.why_matters: Cost, completion, and validity can correlate with task difficulty and arm performance, so calibration for fixed groups may not protect the advertised error rate.
blockers.location: Task 1.8 complete-procedure simulation; Sprint 2 cap and matched-cell degradation risks
blockers.recommendation: Require null simulations of the actual launch order, concurrency, cost reservations, failures, retries, exclusions, and partial-group looks; specify a safe inconclusive outcome when those assumptions fail.

blockers.concern: The plan never states the corpus ceiling. The unseen corpus is sprints 255 … 265 (at most 11 PRs) plus whatever pr-19 … seeds, while the design wants three groups with at least 6 valid PRs per look. Task 1.9 may name an N the corpus cannot supply regardless of budget; the affordable-N rule only handles money.
blockers.why_matters: If N exceeds the available unseen fixtures, the study is underpowered or exploratory by its own rule before any arm runs, and the cycle title ('conclusive') cannot be delivered. Discovering this after annotation spend is wasteful.
blockers.location: Sprint 1 Task 1.1, Task 1.9; Sprint Overview; Risk Register 'Unaffordable N'
blockers.recommendation: Add a corpus-ceiling step to Task 1.1 (count eligible PRs after exposure and review-driven filters) and a rule in Task 1.9/1.11: if the simulated N exceeds the ceiling, state achieved power at the ceiling and declare the study exploratory in PREREGISTRATION.md before annotation starts.

blockers.concern: The registration binds inputs, but the analysis and runner code used for Phase 1 and final reads are not explicitly frozen or governed by a post-registration correction policy.
blockers.why_matters: Changing the decision procedure after interim outcomes are visible can invalidate pre-registration even when REGISTRATION.json remains unchanged.
blockers.recommendation: Bind analysis code, runner code, dependencies, and container digest into the registration; define prospective amendments and bug-fix handling that preserve original outputs and distinguish amended analyses.

blockers.concern: The runner implementation tasks do not explicitly implement the global spend reservation rule, although every batch depends on it.
blockers.why_matters: Recording a cap and overshoot bound does not prevent concurrent sessions, retries, or resumed batches from exceeding the budget.
blockers.recommendation: Assign implementation and tests for an atomic, durable reservation ledger covering concurrent launches, retries, resume, crashes, and settlement of actual costs; refuse launches without sufficient reservation.
